TRREB.kpis: August reads as a balanced market across TRREB, with an SNLR of 37.5% and 4.6 months of inventory sitting near equilibrium. The most useful thing to tell clients is that neither side holds a clear edge right now, so pricing and preparation matter more than timing. Both your buyers and sellers can transact without the pressure of a fast market.
TRREB.price: The average price is $993,410, down 1.1% on the month and down 2.7% year over year, now down 3 months in a row. The median sits at $850,000, down 4.2% from last year. Tell your sellers that recent comparables carry more weight than spring numbers, and let your buyers know the softening is measured, not sudden.
TRREB.balance: With SNLR at 37.5%, up 0.4 points and now up 7 months in a row, absorption is slowly firming even as inventory stays comfortable. That combination keeps leverage close to even at the table. Your buyers have room to negotiate terms, while well priced listings still hold their ground.
TRREB.activity: Sales came in at 5,057, down 2.1% year over year, while new listings fell 14.1% to 12,075 and active listings dropped 11.3% to 24,482. Homes are averaging 51 days on market at 97% of list. The thinner supply tempers the sales dip, so counsel your sellers to price to the market and your buyers to move deliberately on the right fit.

Halton.kpis: Halton is a balanced market, but the momentum has cooled noticeably on price. The clearest message for clients is that supply has pulled back sharply while demand has eased too, keeping the region in equilibrium. Your sellers should expect a longer runway and your buyers should expect real room to negotiate.
Halton.price: The average price is $1,110,436, down 3.6% for the month and down 4.2% year over year, marking 3 straight monthly declines. The median at $957,000 is down 6.1% from last year. Set seller expectations against current comparables, and remind your buyers that the pullback in this price tier is meaningful.
Halton.balance: SNLR sits at 40.0%, up 0.5 points and up 7 months in a row, while months of inventory is 4.2. That points to a market where buyers can press on terms without losing the property to a bidding contest. Prepared sellers who price accurately still command attention.
Halton.activity: Sales of 571 were down 10.2% year over year, and new listings fell 24.7% to 1,201 while active listings dropped 17.3% to 2,413. At 57 days on market and 96% of list, this is a patient market. The steep listing pullback is what keeps it balanced, so guide sellers to sharpen pricing and staging.

Peel.kpis: Peel stands out as a balanced market where sales are actually rising against the trend. The most useful point for clients is that demand held up here even as new supply thinned. That gives your sellers a slightly steadier footing than neighbouring regions while your buyers still have selection.
Peel.price: The average price is $908,415, essentially flat at down 0.2% on the month but down 5.2% year over year. The median holds at $850,000, down 4.5% from last year. Frame the story as prices that have stabilized month to month, and use annual comparables so your sellers price with realistic expectations.
Peel.balance: SNLR is 34.8%, up 0.8 points and up 7 months in a row, while months of inventory sits at 4.9 and has fallen 4 months in a row. Tightening absorption is quietly shifting conditions, though buyers still have negotiating room. Watch this trend closely for your sellers.
Peel.activity: Sales rose 4.7% to 940 even as new listings fell 22.7% to 2,298 and active listings dropped 14.8% to 4,706. Homes average 55 days on market at 97% of list. That mix of rising sales and shrinking supply favors accurately priced listings, so tell your buyers not to assume they hold all the leverage.

Toronto.kpis: Toronto is a balanced market with sales holding almost perfectly flat year over year. The single most useful read for clients is that demand in the city has been steady while supply has tightened. Your buyers face a market that is neither frantic nor stalled, and your sellers benefit from firm underlying activity.
Toronto.price: The average price is $979,684, down 3.1% on the month and down 1.1% year over year, now down 3 months in a row. The median of $770,000 is down 3.7% from last year. The annual softness is mild here, so coach your sellers on realistic pricing and your buyers on measured negotiation.
Toronto.balance: SNLR sits at 38.3%, up 0.2 points and up 7 months in a row, with 4.6 months of inventory. Conditions are even, tilting slightly firmer as absorption improves. Your buyers can still negotiate, but sharply priced listings in the city move without long delays.
Toronto.activity: Sales of 1,767 were down just 0.2% year over year, while new listings fell 7.4% to 4,200 and active listings dropped 9.8% to 8,727. At 46 days on market and 97% of list, Toronto is turning faster than most GTA regions. Tell your buyers that well priced homes here do not linger, and your sellers that presentation pays off.

Durham.kpis: Durham is a balanced market that is running tighter than most of the GTA. The key point for clients is that inventory here is the leanest in the region, which supports pricing despite softer sales. Your sellers hold a firmer position than the balanced label suggests, and your buyers should prepare accordingly.
Durham.price: The average price is $819,569, down 1.8% on the month and down 4.4% year over year. The median at $766,000 is down 4.8% from last year. Use current comparables with your sellers and note to your buyers that the annual pullback has created more accessible entry points in this market.
Durham.balance: SNLR is 41.3%, up 0.2 points and up 6 months in a row, with just 3.4 months of inventory, the tightest of any region here. That balance leans toward sellers at the margin. Advise your buyers to come in with clean, competitive offers on the homes they want.
Durham.activity: Sales of 602 were down 9.5% year over year, while new listings fell 15.1% to 1,423 and active listings dropped 8.7% to 2,467. Homes average 46 days on market at 98% of list, the strongest ratio in the region. That close to list result tells your sellers that accurate pricing gets rewarded here.

Dufferin.kpis: Dufferin is a balanced market and one of the few areas showing gains on both price and sales. Keep in mind this is a small market where monthly figures move sharply, so read the numbers with that context. Still, the direction gives your sellers something positive to point to.
Dufferin.price: The average price is $755,759, up 4.3% on the month and down only 0.5% year over year. The median of $755,378 is up 3.5% from last year, a rare annual gain in this dataset. Tell your sellers the local trend has firmed, while reminding buyers that thin volumes can swing these figures.
Dufferin.balance: SNLR sits at 41.0%, up 1.2 points on the month, the largest monthly gain among these regions, with 4.5 months of inventory. That points to firming demand within a still balanced setting. Your buyers retain negotiating room, but the momentum is moving toward sellers.
Dufferin.activity: Sales rose 7.7% to 28, while new listings fell 24.4% to 59 and active listings dropped 11.7% to 143. Homes average 64 days on market, the longest here, at 97% of list. The long selling time paired with rising sales tells your sellers to price patiently and your buyers to take time on due diligence.

Simcoe.kpis: Simcoe is a balanced market carrying the most inventory in the region and the softest annual price picture. The most useful message for clients is that this is a slower, supply heavy market where buyers have real choice. Your sellers need to compete on price and condition to stand out.
Simcoe.price: The average price is $810,904, down 1.3% on the month and down 9.2% year over year, now down 3 months in a row. The median at $780,000 is down 6.0% from last year. This is the steepest annual pullback among these regions, so ground your sellers firmly in current comparables.
Simcoe.balance: SNLR sits at 32.6%, up 0.3 points and up 6 months in a row, but months of inventory is 6.0, the highest here. That gives your buyers clear leverage at the table. Sellers who overprice will sit, so realistic listing strategy is essential.
Simcoe.activity: Sales of 178 were down 1.7% year over year, while new listings fell 12.6% to 505 and active listings dropped 9.2% to 1,107. Homes average 57 days on market at 97% of list. With ample supply, tell your sellers that sharp pricing drives interest and your buyers that there is no need to rush.
